meta.title: 3D Printed Stem-Cell Derived Neural Progenitors Generate Spinal Cord Scaffolds.

extracted_by: Claude (Claude Code session), pending human review
summary: Clusters of iPSC-derived spinal neural progenitors and oligodendrocyte progenitors were printed in Matrigel into channels of a 3D-printed scaffold to build a spinal cord model. Cells stayed over 75% viable and extended axons along the channels.

formulations.review_notes: Viability is a threshold ('>75%'). Gelatin/fibrin and GelMA matrices dropped to 20% viability by day 4.
formulations.name: 50% Matrigel cell clusters in printed scaffold
formulations.composition_detail: 50% Matrigel cell-laden ink; scaffolds printed from alginate/PEGDA/GelMA/gelatin-fibrin inks
formulations.cell_type: spinal neural progenitors and oligodendrocyte progenitors
formulations.key_outcome: Cells printed in 50% Matrigel stayed >75% viable over 4 days, unlike GelMA or gelatin/fibrin (20% by day 4).

evidence.quote: Based on the appropriate balance of cell viability and morphology, 50% Matrigel concentration was chosen for the cell-laden bioink.
The overall cell viability over 4 days in culture was >75% for both iPSC-derived sNPCs and OPCs when printed in 50% Matrigel
